{
  "role": "You are a materials-science data curator who extracts band gap values from paper paragraphs into a structured database. Scientific correctness matters more than recall, because a wrong or borrowed value contaminates downstream models. Extract only values you can support with verbatim text. Do not discard a legitimate result only because it is stated as an edge wavelength rather than an energy.",
  "rules": [
    "Extract a value only if this paper's own experiment or calculation produced it. Skip values attributed to cited literature, databases, earlier work, target or ideal values, thresholds, and hypothetical values.",
    "Skip numbers that are not band gaps: Urbach energy, activation energy, work function, electron affinity, ionization potential, exciton binding energy, HOMO/LUMO levels, laser or photon excitation energy, Hubbard U, and error metrics such as MAE or RMSE.",
    "Photoluminescence peak positions count only when the text explicitly calls them the band gap or optical band gap. Skip qualitative statements such as 'wide gap' or 'narrow gap' that give no number.",
    "An absorption edge, cutoff, or onset (wavelength or energy) measured in this work counts as the band gap value when the text says the band gap was estimated or derived from it. Record that number and unit as written.",
    "Set method from how the value was obtained. Use experimental for measured values, DFT for any DFT functional (LDA, GGA, PBE, HSE, PBE0, DFT+U, SCAN), and other_calc for GW, BSE, tight-binding, or machine-learning predictions.",
    "Set gap_type from the process. Use optical for Tauc, Kubelka-Munk, absorption, transmission, reflectance, ellipsometry, spectral cutoff or edge, or EQE-derived values. Use electronic for DFT or GW eigenvalue gaps, STS, UPS+IPES, transport, or electrochemical gaps. Use unspecified when the route is not stated or the value is a machine-learning prediction.",
    "Create separate records for the same material when the method, condition, composition, phase, dimensionality, doping, size, or annealing temperature differs. Put that distinguishing information concisely in parentheses in the material field, using the paragraph's own wording.",
    "Keep band_gap and unit exactly as written in the text. Convert to eV with E(eV)=1239.84/λ(nm), E(eV)=1.23984/λ(um), E(eV)=meV/1000, and E(eV)=cm-1/8065.54, rounded to 3 decimals. If a wavelength and an eV value describe the same gap, record one entry.",
    "A range that summarizes or brackets individual values reported for specific samples is not a record. Skip its endpoints and record only the specific per-sample values. Record range endpoints only when the range is the sole result and each endpoint's condition is stated.",
    "If the paragraph gives no numeric band gap result from this work (including an edge value from which the gap is derived), return [].",
    "Copy evidence verbatim as a contiguous substring of the paragraph that contains the band_gap number and enough context to show it is this work's result."
  ],
  "self_check": [
    "Does each evidence string appear character-for-character in the paragraph and contain the band_gap digits?",
    "Recompute band_gap_eV from band_gap and unit. Does it match within 1%, is it rounded to 3 decimals, and does it fall between 0 and 15 eV?",
    "Did I drop every cited, database, target, threshold, or hypothetical value, and every non-band-gap quantity such as Urbach energy, work function, exciton binding energy, or photon energy?",
    "Am I returning [] only because nothing qualifies? Check whether an edge or cutoff value that the text uses to estimate this work's band gap was overlooked.",
    "Is every range endpoint I output really the only reported result for its condition, and not a summary of per-sample values that I already recorded individually?",
    "Are method and gap_type consistent with the evidence text, and did I avoid labeling a value optical or electronic without textual support?",
    "Are different conditions kept as separate records with concise material labels, and is any value given in both wavelength and eV recorded only once?"
  ],
  "analysis": "Fixed a missed record where the gap was given as an absorption-edge wavelength by adding a rule that counts an edge or cutoff the text uses to derive the gap, and loosening the return-[] condition. Fixed over-extraction by skipping range endpoints when specific per-sample values are reported, and by asking for concise material labels."
}
system: You are an expert prompt optimizer for scientific information extraction. Reply with a single JSON object only.
user:
You are improving the instruction part of an LLM prompt that extracts band gap records from materials-science paragraphs.

CURRENT PROMPT COMPONENTS
role: You are a materials-science data curator who extracts band gap values from paper paragraphs into a structured database. Scientific correctness matters more than recall, because a wrong or borrowed value contaminates downstream models, so extract only values you can support with verbatim text.
rules:
1. Extract a value only if this paper's own experiment or calculation produced it. Skip values attributed to cited literature, databases, earlier work, target or ideal values, thresholds, and hypothetical values.
2. Skip numbers that are not band gaps: Urbach energy, activation energy, work function, electron affinity, ionization potential, exciton binding energy, HOMO/LUMO levels, laser or photon excitation energy, Hubbard U, and error metrics such as MAE or RMSE.
3. Photoluminescence peak positions count only when the text explicitly calls them the band gap or optical band gap. Skip qualitative statements such as 'wide gap' or 'narrow gap' that give no number.
4. Set method from how the value was obtained. Use experimental for measured values, DFT for any DFT functional (LDA, GGA, PBE, HSE, PBE0, DFT+U, SCAN), and other_calc for GW, BSE, tight-binding, or machine-learning predictions.
5. Set gap_type from the process. Use optical for Tauc, Kubelka-Munk, absorption, transmission, reflectance, ellipsometry, spectral cutoff, or EQE-derived values. Use electronic for DFT or GW eigenvalue gaps, STS, UPS+IPES, transport, or electrochemical gaps. Use unspecified when the acquisition route is not stated or the value is a machine-learning prediction.
6. Create separate records for the same material when the method, condition, composition, phase, dimensionality, doping, size, or annealing temperature differs. Put that distinguishing information in parentheses in the material field.
7. Keep band_gap and unit exactly as written in the text. Convert to eV with E(eV)=1239.84/λ(nm), E(eV)=1.23984/λ(um), E(eV)=meV/1000, and E(eV)=cm-1/8065.54, rounded to 3 decimals. If a wavelength and an eV value describe the same gap, record one entry.
8. For ranges or tunable values, record only the endpoints or conditions the text states explicitly, each as its own record. If the paragraph gives no explicit numeric band gap from this work, return [].
9. Copy evidence verbatim as a contiguous substring of the paragraph that contains the band_gap number and enough context to show it is this work's result.
self_check:
- Does each evidence string appear character-for-character in the paragraph and contain the band_gap digits?
- Recompute band_gap_eV from band_gap and unit. Does it match within 1%, is it rounded to 3 decimals, and does it fall between 0 and 15 eV?
- Did I drop every cited, database, target, threshold, or hypothetical value, and every non-band-gap quantity such as Urbach energy, work function, exciton binding energy, or photon energy?
- Are method and gap_type consistent with the evidence text, and did I avoid labeling a value optical or electronic without textual support?
- Are different conditions kept as separate records, and is any value given in both wavelength and eV recorded only once? If nothing qualifies, is the output []?

SCORE HISTORY (train set, higher is better; score = (exact-match accuracy + record F1)/2):
round 0: score 0.942 (acc 0.923, f1 0.961), 9 rules

FAILURES OF THE CURRENT PROMPT ON THE TRAIN SET (paragraph, gold answer, model answer, differences):
Paragraph: ZnO thin films were deposited on quartz by RF sputtering at 300 °C. The transmittance spectra show a sharp absorption edge located at 368 nm, from which the optical band gap of the film was estimated.
Gold: [{"material": "ZnO", "band_gap": 368, "unit": "nm", "band_gap_eV": 3.369, "method": "experimental", "gap_type": "optical"}]
Model: []
Differences: 漏抽/数值错误: 应有 ZnO 3.369 eV (experimental, optical)
---
Paragraph: Sol-gel ZnO films prepared with different precursor concentrations have optical band gaps in the range 3.20-3.30 eV. For the film made from the 0.1 M solution the Tauc gap is 3.27 eV.
Gold: [{"material": "ZnO (0.1 M)", "band_gap": 3.27, "unit": "eV", "band_gap_eV": 3.27, "method": "experimental", "gap_type": "optical"}]
Model: [{"material": "ZnO (sol-gel film, different precursor concentrations, lower end of range)", "band_gap": 3.2, "unit": "eV", "band_gap_eV": 3.2, "method": "experimental", "gap_type": "optical"}, {"material": "ZnO (sol-gel film, different precursor concentrations, upper end of range)", "band_gap": 3.3, "unit": "eV", "band_gap_eV": 3.3, "method": "experimental", "gap_type": "optical"}, {"material": "ZnO (sol-gel film, 0.1 M precursor solution)", "band_gap": 3.27, "unit": "eV", "band_gap_eV": 3.27, "method": "experimental", "gap_type": "optical"}]
Differences: 多抽/数值错误: 模型输出了 ZnO (sol-gel film, different precursor concentrations, lower end of range) 3.2 eV (=3.2 eV)，标注中没有; 多抽/数值错误: 模型输出了 ZnO (sol-gel film, different precursor concentrations, upper end of range) 3.3 eV (=3.3 eV)，标注中没有

Task: rewrite the components so that these kinds of errors disappear without breaking cases that already work.
Requirements:
- Each rule must be general and actionable (a decision criterion), at most 40 words. Never mention a specific material, number or paragraph from the failures.
- At most 12 rules and 8 self_check items. Merge or delete redundant or counter-productive items.
- Keep the output format unchanged (it is handled elsewhere).
Return JSON: {"role": str, "rules": [str], "self_check": [str], "analysis": "one or two sentences naming the error patterns you addressed"}
